Regarding the text provided: "Each of the workers received their paycheck on Friday. It ensures that they have them before the weekend."

There is a pronoun-antecedent agreement error in the second sentence. The pronoun "It" is singular, but it refers to the plural concept of the paychecks or the situation involving multiple workers. Additionally, "them" is plural, which agrees with "workers," but the first part of the sentence is awkward. A clearer correction focusing on agreement would be:

"Each of the workers received their paycheck on Friday. This ensures that they have it before the weekend."

Alternatively, to maintain strict singular agreement with "Each":

"Each of the workers received his or her paycheck on Friday. This ensures that he or she has it before the weekend."

However, using singular "they" is widely accepted in modern usage. The main error is the use of "It" to refer to the action or the paychecks. A better correction is:

"Each of the workers received their paycheck on Friday. This ensures that they have it before the weekend."
